context.body: A foreign ruler’s victories are placed inside God’s purpose for Israel and public recognition.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: The LORD calls Cyrus anointed, subdues nations, names and equips him, declares sole deity, and claims light, darkness, well-being, and calamity.
observations.label: God calls Cyrus without being known by him: action

observations.body: Cyrus acts as an instrument before he knows the God who names him.
observations.label: God calls Cyrus without being known by him: response

observations.body: anointed · though you have not known me · no other · create calamity
observations.label: Words in Isaiah 45:1–13

payload.posture: Read Isaiah 45:1–13 as the prophetic voice evidence before carrying it into another source.
payload.tension: The claim about creating calamity requires attention to the passage’s political-judgment setting and cannot be flattened into every evil act.
payload.title: God calls Cyrus without being known by him
